question: Do government/enterprise procurement texts (2025-2026) require what AEGIS offers: memory-safe language, FIPS 140-3 validated module, PQC/CNSA 2.0 timelines, formal verification / SA-17(1), SBOM, SLSA provenance, reproducible builds? Test the claim 'buyers don't ask for assurance'.
flips_if: D-13 flip: procurement scoring evidence (q4-003). P-2 reverse: procurement texts (RFPs, STIGs) score PQ, memory safety or formal assurance for gateways.

measured.corpus: 25 documents scored (22 policy/framework/questionnaire texts + 3 real proxy/WAF tenders), dated 2025-01 to 2026-10, US federal/DoD/NSS, EU, UK, FR, AU, CA, CH, CO, plus 2 enterprise questionnaires. SIG 2026 found but not verifiable, excluded. Table: spikes/q4-003/scores.csv. Accessed 2026-10-25.

tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.memory_safe_language: 0 / 2 / 0 / 23 (only binding-ish text: ASD ISM-1826 vendor selection for server applications; US CISA/NSA is voluntary developer guidance)
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.FIPS_140_validated_module: 4 / 2 / 0 / 19 (MUST: Canada contract clauses from 2026-04-01, DISA Web Server SRG CAT I, CNSSP-15/NIAP for NSS, EO 14412 FAR rule (proposed, due ~2026-12, compliance 2030-12-31); SHOULD: FedRAMP CR26 Class C, ASD ISM-1990 'preferred')
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.PQC_with_dates: 5 / 5 / 0 / 15 (MUST: EO 14412 2030/2031, OMB M-26-15 names 'API proxies' and 'API gateways' explicitly, CNSSP-15 NSS acquisitions 2027-01-01, Canada contracts 2026-04-01, ANSSI qualification 2027 (announced); SHOULD: CISA web servers 'acquire only PQC-capable', EU 2030/2035, NCSC 2028/2031/2035, ASD ISM-1917 by 2030, AusCERT scored questionnaire)
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.formal_verification_or_SA17_1: 0 / 0 / 1 / 24 (SA-17(1) is in no NIST 800-53B baseline; SA-17 base only in High; SSDF 1.2 draft lists formal methods as an optional example)
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.SBOM: 1 / 6 / 1 / 17 (MUST: EU CRA Annex I Part II(1), applies 2027-12-11; US federal SBOM mandate rescinded by M-26-05 to 'may require on request')
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.SLSA_or_build_provenance: 0 / 2 / 0 / 23 (ASD ISM-2056; SSDF PS.3.2; SLSA not named anywhere)
tallies_MUST_SHOULD_MAYexample_absent_of.CBOM: 0 / 2 / 0 / 23 + 1 forthcoming (ASD ISM-2083, AusCERT scored; CISA CBOM minimum elements due ~2027-03 under EO 14412)

measured.real_tenders: 3 of 3 real WAF/reverse-proxy tenders (Colombia 2025-08, Coquitlam 2025-04, UZH 2026-06) ask for none of the seven; they ask OWASP Top 10, ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, SIEM/firewall integration, and the UZH incumbent is Apache httpd + ModSecurity (C).
measured.claim_test: 'Buyers don't ask for assurance' is TRUE for formal verification (0 MUST, 0 SHOULD) and mostly true for memory safety (0 MUST; one jurisdiction SHOULD). It is FALSE for crypto and supply-chain compliance: PQC appears with dated MUSTs in 5 texts and names proxies/gateways explicitly (M-26-15), FIPS-validated modules gate DoD/NSS/Canada, SBOM gates EU CRA.

decision_effect: D-13 changes from 'invisible assurance, parity first' to 'visible compliance, invisible proofs': (1) Sales/positioning copy leads with PQC-by-default (ML-KEM-1024 hybrid 0x11ED matches CNSA 2.0 and ASD ISM-1917/1995 parameter preference), a FIPS 140-3 profile, and SBOM + CBOM + build provenance + reproducible build as release artefacts. Formal verification and memory safety stay out of procurement copy and appear only as engineering evidence (claim ledger, NOT-proven list). P-2 reverse fires for PQ (not for memory safety or formal assurance). (2) R-GAP-4 column (f) 'machine-checked claims' is not a procurement differentiator; do not justify it by demand. (3) Phase 6 split: FIPS/jurisdiction profiles, 0x11ED, reproducible signed release are procurement-gating for US-federal/DoD/NSS/Canada/EU and are justified by demand; the Lean selection-model gate is not procurement-driven (justify on safety grounds only). (4) Move SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX, CRA top-level deps minimum), CBOM and SLSA provenance from Phase 6 into the Phase 2 first shippable release: they are cheap and CRA SBOM is a MUST from 2027-12-11. (5) Phases 4-5 (data plane, P2 isolation) are neither required nor scored by any procurement text: their go/no-go must rest on the agent-infra segment evidence and post-Phase-2 velocity, not on q4-003. (6) M-26-15 asks for configuration-driven crypto 'not compiled into the application binary' (as an agility option): within each lock profile, KX group and sigalg lists in F12 must be runtime-selectable by config; only the FIPS boundary itself stays compile-time (D-11), documented as the reason.
rung: Measurement grade B (primary texts A where fetched; corpus is purposive, not random; framework texts over-represent regulators; 3 real tenders are small buyers).
reproduce: Open each URL in spikes/q4-003/scores.csv (accessed 2026-10-25) and grep for the seven features. Mechanical checks: NIST baselines: curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_HIGH-baseline_profile.json | grep -o '"sa-17[^"]*"' | sort -u   (prints only "sa-17"). ASD ISM: curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AustralianCyberSecurityCentre/ism-oscal/v2026.09.4/ISM_catalog.json and search controls ism-1826, ism-1917, ism-1990, ism-1730, ism-2056, ism-2155, ism-2083. EO 14412 / M-26-15 / M-26-05: pdftotext the whitehouse.gov PDFs and grep 'proxies|gateways|2030|SBOM'.
limits: Purposive sample, not a random draw of procurement actions; real federal RFP texts (SAM.gov) were not retrievable and none for proxies/gateways were found; enterprise questionnaires SIG 2026 and Microsoft SSPA DPR v12 could not be read (paywall/unverified); CNSA 2.0/CNSSP-15 primaries returned 403 (graded B from secondary consensus); EUR-Lex was bot-blocked (CRA read via mirror); ANSSI 2027 date is an announced aim ('vise'), not a published rule; EO 14412 FAR rules are not yet proposed (due ~2026-12-19 and ~2027-03); FedRAMP CR26 softened FIPS to SHOULD for Class C, so FIPS gating in federal cloud is weaker than DoD/NSS. Text requirements are not purchase behaviour: no data on how often these clauses decide awards.
